title: Body Water, Electrolytes and Acid–Base: The PCP's Why
next: Chapter 6, Lesson 2: Shock inside the cell, immunity, inflammation and allergy

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already read skin, mental status and breathing, and you give oxygen and oral glucose. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Where body water lives and how it moves — the science of your IV bag
  2. Read electrolyte and acid–base problems on scene
  3. How cells are injured, and what the PCP adds for fluid loss

Textbook: Chapter 6, PDF pages 314–377
slides.say: Welcome back. Pathophysiology simply means how the body works when it is sick or injured. Disease starts when the body's balance, called homeostasis, breaks. As an EMR you already read skin, mental status and breathing, and you give oxygen and oral glucose. Now that you're practising as a PCP, you can put fluid and drugs straight into a vein, so you must know what that fluid does once it's inside. Today: where body water lives and how it moves, how to read electrolyte and acid–base problems on scene, and how cells get injured.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。病理生理学，说白了就是身体生病或受伤时是怎么运转的。身体的平衡叫稳态，平衡一被打破，疾病就开始了。作为 EMR，你已经会看皮肤、神志和呼吸，也会给氧、给口服葡萄糖。现在以 PCP 身份执业，你可以把液体和药物直接输进静脉，所以必须知道液体进去以后会做什么。今天讲：身体的水在哪里、怎么流动；在现场怎么看出电解质和酸碱问题；细胞怎样受损。

slides.title: Where the body's water lives
slides.body:
Body water ≈ 60% of weight (average man)

Where% of body weight
Inside cells45%
Between cells (interstitial)10.5%
Inside vessels (intravascular)4.5%

Woman ≈ 50% · term newborn ≈ 80% · older adult as low as 45%. A healthy adult gets ill after losing > 30% of body fluid; a small child shows symptoms at 10–15%.
slides.say: About sixty percent of an average man's weight is water, and about fifty percent of a woman's. Most of it, forty-five percent of body weight, sits inside the cells. Ten and a half percent sits between the cells; that's interstitial fluid. Only four and a half percent is inside the blood vessels. So the blood is a small pool joined to two much bigger ones. A term newborn is about eighty percent water, an older adult as low as forty-five. And a healthy adult must lose more than thirty percent of body fluid to become ill, but a small child shows symptoms after only ten to fifteen percent.
slides.sayZh: 一般男性体重约百分之六十是水，女性约百分之五十。大部分，也就是体重的百分之四十五，在细胞里；百分之十点五在细胞之间，叫组织间液；只有百分之四点五在血管里。所以血液只是一个小水池，连着两个大得多的水池。足月新生儿约百分之八十是水，老人可低到百分之四十五。健康成人要丢失超过百分之三十的体液才会生病，而小孩只丢百分之十到十五就会出现症状。

slides.title: Tonicity: what your IV bag does
slides.body:
Isotonicsame as cell fluid (≈ 280 mOsm/L)0.9% NaCl, lactated Ringer
Hypertonicpulls water out of cellscells shrink
Hypotoniclets water into cellscells swell

Water moves by osmosis toward the side with more dissolved particles. The Na⁺/K⁺ pump sends 3 Na⁺ out for every 2 K⁺ in, using energy, so cells don't swell.
slides.say: Water moves between these pools mainly by osmosis, which means water travels toward the side with more dissolved particles. Tonicity compares a fluid with the inside of a cell, which is about two hundred eighty milliosmoles per litre. An isotonic fluid matches it, so cells neither shrink nor swell. Normal saline and lactated Ringer's are isotonic, so they refill volume without upsetting the cells. A hypertonic fluid pulls water out of cells; hospitals use it to shrink a swollen brain. A hypotonic fluid lets water into cells. And inside every cell, the sodium–potassium pump spends energy to keep the cell from swelling.
slides.sayZh: 水在这几个水池之间主要靠渗透移动，也就是水往溶质更多的一侧走。张力是拿液体和细胞内部作比较，细胞内约每升二百八十毫渗量。等渗液与之相同，细胞既不皱缩也不肿胀；生理盐水和乳酸林格液都是等渗的，所以能补充容量又不扰乱细胞。高渗液把水从细胞里拉出来，医院用它给肿胀的大脑脱水。低渗液则让水进入细胞。每个细胞里还有钠钾泵，消耗能量来防止细胞肿胀。

slides.title: Starling forces: why fluid leaks
slides.body:
• Capillary pressure pushes water out into the tissues
  • Plasma proteins (mainly albumin) hold water in
  • Balance lost → fluid pools between cells = edema
Pressure ↑heart failure, blocked veinspushes more out
Protein ↓liver disease, starvation, big burnscan't hold water
Lymph blockednodes removed, infectionno drainage
slides.say: Fluid also moves between the blood and the tissues; these are called Starling forces. Pressure inside the capillary pushes water out. Plasma proteins, mainly albumin, hold water in, like a sponge. Edema, which means extra fluid in the tissues, appears when that balance breaks. There are three main causes: the pushing pressure rises, as in heart failure; there's too little protein to hold water, as in liver disease, starvation or large burns; or the lymph drainage is blocked. When edema forms in the lungs, oxygen can't cross into the blood, and the patient becomes hypoxic. That's why a PCP listens to the lungs before and during any fluid bolus.
slides.sayZh: 液体还会在血液和组织之间移动，这叫 Starling 力。毛细血管里的压力把水往外推；血浆蛋白，主要是白蛋白，像海绵一样把水留住。这个平衡被打破，组织里液体过多，就是水肿。三个主要原因：往外推的压力升高，比如心衰；蛋白太少留不住水，比如肝病、饥饿或大面积烧伤；或者淋巴引流被堵。水肿发生在肺里，氧气进不了血液，病人就会缺氧。所以 PCP 在推注补液前和补液中都要听肺。

slides.q: You're a PCP giving a fluid bolus to a hypotensive patient with a history of heart failure. After 500 mL you hear new crackles at both lung bases, and breathing is harder. Best interpretation?
options: The bolus is working; continue to 2 L
Fluid is leaking into the lungs; reassess before giving more
Crackles are a normal sound after saline
The patient needs a hypertonic fluid instead
slides.say: You're a PCP giving a fluid bolus to a hypotensive patient with a history of heart failure. After five hundred millilitres, you hear new crackles at both lung bases, and the breathing is harder. What is the best interpretation? A, the bolus is working; continue to two litres. B, fluid is leaking into the lungs; reassess before giving more. C, crackles are a normal sound after saline. D, the patient needs a hypertonic fluid instead. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 你是 PCP，正在给一位有心衰史的低血压病人推注补液。输了五百毫升后，你在双肺底听到新出现的湿啰音，呼吸也更费力了。最合理的解读是什么？A，补液起效了，继续输到两升；B，液体正在渗进肺里，再给之前先复评；C，输生理盐水后出现湿啰音是正常的；D，病人需要改用高渗液。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. In heart failure, the pressure in the lung capillaries is already high, so extra volume can push fluid into the lungs. New crackles and harder breathing are a warning sign, and that is why reassessing every five hundred millilitres matters. A ignores the warning. C is wrong; crackles mean fluid in the small airways. D doesn't help, because the real problem is too much fluid in the lungs, not the kind of bag.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。心衰病人肺毛细血管的压力本来就高，多给的容量会把液体推进肺里。新出现的湿啰音和更费力的呼吸是警讯，这正是每五百毫升复评一次的意义。A 无视了警讯；C 错，湿啰音说明小气道里有液体；D 没用，因为真正的问题是肺里液体太多，而不是用哪种液体。

slides.title: Salt and water: the body's own IV
slides.body:
• Thirst and ADH are the main water controls
  • Blood too concentrated → ADH → kidneys keep water
  • Pressure or kidney flow drops → RAAS → kidneys keep sodium
  • Sodium is the main cation outside cells; water follows it
  • Dry patient: dizzy on standing, little urine
  • Sodium far too high or low → confusion, seizures, coma
slides.say: The two main water controls are thirst and ADH, or antidiuretic hormone. When the blood gets too concentrated, the brain releases ADH, and the kidneys hold on to water. When blood pressure or kidney blood flow drops, the kidneys start a hormone chain called RAAS, the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system. It holds on to sodium, and water follows the sodium. It's the same system that props up blood pressure in shock. If the patient is still dry, you'll see dizziness on standing and very little urine. When sodium goes far too high or too low, the brain suffers: confusion, seizures, even coma.
slides.sayZh: 调节水分最主要的两个开关是口渴和 ADH，即抗利尿激素。血液太浓时，大脑释放 ADH，肾脏就留住水。血压或肾血流下降时，肾脏启动一条激素链，叫 RAAS，即肾素-血管紧张素-醛固酮系统，它留住钠，水跟着钠走。休克时撑住血压的也是这套系统。病人如果仍然缺水，你会看到站起来头晕、尿很少。血钠过高或过低，大脑就会受害：意识混乱、抽搐，甚至昏迷。

slides.title: Potassium: the heart's electrolyte
slides.body:
Normal K⁺: 3.5–5.0 mEq/L

  • Low (vomiting, diarrhea, diuretics): weakness, cramps, dysrhythmias
  • High (kidney failure, some drugs, burns, acidosis): dysrhythmias
  • High K⁺ ECG clues: peaked T waves, wide QRS
  • Fewer than half show ECG changes, even above 6.5
  • Book's IV calcium, bicarbonate, insulin: not on the BC exam
  • Salbutamol is on the BC list for bronchospasm, not potassium
slides.say: Potassium is the main electrolyte inside cells, and its normal blood range is narrow: three point five to five point zero. Low potassium comes from losses like vomiting, diarrhea or diuretics, and causes weakness, cramps and rhythm problems. High potassium comes from kidney failure, some drugs, burns or acidosis, and it kills through the heart. Classic ECG clues are peaked T waves and a wide QRS, yet fewer than half of patients show changes even above six point five. The book's treatments, IV calcium, bicarbonate and insulin, aren't on the BC licensing exam. Your job is to suspect it from the history, and move.
slides.sayZh: 钾是细胞内最主要的电解质，正常血钾范围很窄：三点五到五点零。低钾来自呕吐、腹泻、利尿剂等丢失，引起乏力、抽筋和心律失常。高钾来自肾衰、某些药物、烧伤或酸中毒，会通过心脏致命。典型心电图线索是 T 波高尖、QRS 增宽，但即使血钾超过六点五，出现心电图改变的也不到一半。书里的治疗——静脉钙、碳酸氢盐、胰岛素——都不在 BC 执照考试范围内。你的任务是从病史中想到它，然后尽快行动。

slides.title: Acid–base: pH and the buffer
slides.body:
Normal blood pH: 7.35–7.45

acid + bicarbonate→carbonic acid→water + CO₂ breathed out
  • Lungs adjust fast; kidneys take hours to days
  • Acidosis (< 7.35): brain slows → confusion → breathing stops
  • Alkalosis (> 7.45): nerves over-fire → tingling → twitching → spasm
slides.say: Blood pH must stay between seven point three five and seven point four five. The main defence is the bicarbonate buffer. Think of bicarbonate as a sponge for acid. It grabs the acid and turns it into carbonic acid, which splits into water and carbon dioxide, and you breathe the carbon dioxide out. So the lungs are an exhaust pipe for acid. They adjust quickly, while the kidneys need hours to days. Below seven point three five is acidosis: the brain slows, the patient gets confused, and finally breathing stops. Above seven point four five is alkalosis: nerves over-fire, causing tingling, then twitching, then spasm.
slides.sayZh: 血液 pH 必须保持在七点三五到七点四五之间。主要防线是碳酸氢盐缓冲系统。把碳酸氢根想成吸酸的海绵：它抓住酸，变成碳酸，碳酸分解成水和二氧化碳，二氧化碳被呼出去。所以肺就是酸的排气管。肺调节很快，肾脏要几小时到几天。低于七点三五是酸中毒：大脑变慢，病人意识混乱，最后呼吸停止。高于七点四五是碱中毒：神经过度兴奋，先是麻刺感，再是抽动，然后痉挛。

slides.title: Four acid–base problems
slides.body:
ProblemTypical causesBreathing clue
Respiratory acidosisopioid overdose, asthma, COPDslow or weak
Respiratory alkalosisPE, heart attack, severe infectionfast — find the cause
Metabolic acidosisDKA, sepsis, ASA overdosedeep and fast (Kussmaul)
Metabolic alkalosisvomiting, NG suction, antacidsslower over time

Acidosis pushes potassium up. Acute compensation is never complete.
slides.say: When carbon dioxide is retained, as in an opioid overdose, severe asthma or COPD, you get respiratory acidosis. When it's blown off too fast, you get respiratory alkalosis. Don't assume anxiety: a pulmonary embolism, a heart attack or a severe infection can all drive fast breathing. In diabetic ketoacidosis, sepsis or an aspirin overdose, acids build up: that's metabolic acidosis. The lungs compensate with deep, fast Kussmaul breathing to blow off carbon dioxide, so don't try to slow it down. Vomiting removes stomach acid and can cause metabolic alkalosis. And acidosis tends to push potassium up, so watch the heart.
slides.sayZh: 二氧化碳潴留，比如阿片过量、严重哮喘或 COPD，就是呼吸性酸中毒。二氧化碳呼出太快，是呼吸性碱中毒；别想当然归为焦虑：肺栓塞、心梗或严重感染都会让人呼吸加快。糖尿病酮症酸中毒、脓毒症或阿司匹林过量时，酸在体内堆积，这是代谢性酸中毒；肺会用深而快的 Kussmaul 呼吸排出二氧化碳来代偿，所以别试图让它慢下来。呕吐丢失胃酸，可以造成代谢性碱中毒。另外，酸中毒往往让血钾升高，所以要盯住心脏。

slides.q: You find a man after a heroin overdose: breathing 6 times a minute and shallow, SpO₂ 82%. Which problem is building, and what comes first?
options: Metabolic acidosis — give a fluid bolus first
Respiratory acidosis — ventilate with BVM and oxygen, then naloxone
Respiratory alkalosis — coach him to breathe slowly
Metabolic alkalosis — give naloxone, then wait before ventilating
slides.say: Second question. You find a man after a heroin overdose. He's breathing six times a minute and shallow, and his oxygen saturation is eighty-two percent. Which problem is building, and what comes first? A, metabolic acidosis; give a fluid bolus first. B, respiratory acidosis; ventilate with a bag-valve mask and oxygen, then give naloxone. C, respiratory alkalosis; coach him to breathe slowly. D, metabolic alkalosis; give naloxone, then wait before ventilating. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 第二题。你发现一名海洛因过量的男子，每分钟呼吸六次、很浅，血氧饱和度百分之八十二。正在形成的是哪种问题？第一步做什么？A，代谢性酸中毒，先推注补液；B，呼吸性酸中毒，先用球囊面罩加氧通气，再给纳洛酮；C，呼吸性碱中毒，指导他慢慢呼吸；D，代谢性碱中毒，先给纳洛酮，等一等再通气。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Slow, shallow breathing holds on to carbon dioxide, so this is respiratory acidosis, and the fix is ventilation. In BC you secure ventilation first, then give naloxone: zero point four milligrams, then zero point four, zero point eight, and two milligrams, reassessing every three minutes, or four milligrams in the nose. As a PCP, if he stays unconscious and apneic, you can also consider giving it through an IV. A treats the wrong problem, C is the opposite problem, and D delays the breaths he needs right now.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。呼吸慢而浅会让二氧化碳潴留，所以是呼吸性酸中毒，对策是通气。BC 规定先保证通气，再给纳洛酮：零点四毫克，然后零点四、零点八、二毫克，每三分钟评估一次；或者经鼻给四毫克。作为 PCP，如果他持续昏迷、没有呼吸，还可以考虑经静脉给药。A 治错了问题；C 是相反的问题；D 耽误了他此刻最需要的通气。

slides.title: Cell injury: from hypoxia to cell death
slides.body:
• Main cause: hypoxia; also ischemia, chemicals, infection, immune
  • No oxygen → little energy → pumps fail → cell swells
  • Hypoxic cells release free radicals → more damage, more hypoxia
  • Reversible early; past a certain point, the cell dies
  • Acetaminophen > 140 mg/kg (adult) → liver injury
  • BC acetaminophen limit: 4,000 mg per 24 h, all sources
slides.say: Cells can be injured by lack of oxygen, poor blood flow, chemicals, infection, the immune system, physical force or inflammation. Lack of oxygen, or hypoxia, is the most common. Without oxygen the cell makes little energy, its pumps fail, sodium and water rush in, and it swells. Hypoxic cells also release free radicals, unstable molecules that attack nearby membranes and cause more hypoxia: a vicious circle. Early damage can be reversed; past a certain point, nothing helps. That's why oxygen, ventilation and perfusion are urgent. Chemicals injure cells too: over one hundred forty milligrams per kilogram of acetaminophen poisons an adult's liver, so ask about every source; the BC limit is four thousand milligrams a day.
slides.sayZh: 细胞受损的原因有缺氧、血流不足、化学物质、感染、免疫系统、外力和炎症，其中缺氧最常见。没有氧，细胞几乎产生不了能量，泵就停了，钠和水涌进去，细胞肿胀。缺氧的细胞还会释放自由基，这种不稳定的分子攻击附近的细胞膜，造成更多缺氧，形成恶性循环。早期损伤可以逆转，过了某个点就无药可救。所以给氧、通气和灌注都刻不容缓。化学物质同样伤细胞：成人对乙酰氨基酚超过每公斤一百四十毫克就会毒害肝脏，所以要问清所有来源；BC 的上限是每天四千毫克。

slides.title: Genes and family history
slides.body:
• Disease risk = genes + environment + age + sex
  • Dominant: one gene copy is enough → each child ≥ 50% chance
  • Recessive: two copies needed → two carrier parents, 25% per child
  • Father: MI before 55, or mother: MI before 65 → higher cardiac risk

Treat fainting as a deadly rhythm until proven otherwise if it happens: during exercise · with chest pain · when a close relative also faints · after a sudden fright or loud noise
slides.say: Disease risk comes from genes, environment, age and sex. In autosomal dominant conditions, one faulty copy of a gene is enough, so each child has at least a fifty percent chance. In autosomal recessive conditions, a person needs two copies, so two carrier parents have a twenty-five percent chance with each child. Family history changes how you read a patient. A father with a heart attack before fifty-five, or a mother before sixty-five, raises cardiac risk. And inherited rhythm problems like long QT syndrome can cause sudden death, so some faints must be treated as a deadly rhythm until proven otherwise.
slides.sayZh: 患病风险来自基因、环境、年龄和性别。常染色体显性遗传，一份致病基因就够，每个孩子至少有百分之五十的机会；常染色体隐性遗传，要两份才发病，父母都是携带者时，每个孩子有百分之二十五的机会。家族史会改变你对病人的判断。父亲五十五岁前心梗，或母亲六十五岁前心梗，心脏风险就更高。像长 QT 综合征这样的遗传性心律问题可以导致猝死，所以有些晕厥必须先按致命性心律失常处理，直到排除为止。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: fluid lost from vomiting
slides.body:
BC Nausea–Vomiting protocol. Vomiting and diarrhea drain water, sodium and potassium.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Rest in a position of comfort
  • Position to protect the airway
  • Expect vomiting; have suction ready

PCP adds

  • Consider vascular access (IV)
  • Consider dimenhydrinate or ondansetron
  • Hypotension from volume loss: bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL; target systolic 90
  • Stable: antiemetic on scene. Unstable: en route
slides.say: Vomiting and diarrhea drain water, sodium and potassium, and BC has a protocol for it. The left column is what every licence level does: rest the patient in a position of comfort, position them to protect the airway, and keep suction ready. The right column is new for you. The PCP may start an IV and may give dimenhydrinate or ondansetron for the nausea. If the patient is hypotensive from volume loss, you give a fluid bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, with a target systolic of ninety. A stable patient can have the antiemetic on scene; an unstable patient gets it en route.
slides.sayZh: 呕吐和腹泻会丢失水、钠和钾，BC 对此有专门流程。左栏是所有执照级别都做的：让病人在舒适体位休息，摆好体位保护气道，备好吸引器。右栏对你是新的：PCP 可以开静脉通路，可以给茶苯海明或昂丹司琼止吐。如果病人因丢失容量而低血压，按每公斤二十毫升推注补液，最多两升，每五百毫升复评一次，目标收缩压九十。稳定的病人可以在现场给止吐药，不稳定的在转运途中给。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Listen to the lungs before and during a bolus (≥ 6 sites, front or back)
  • New crackles or harder breathing → reassess before more fluid
  • Heart, kidney or liver failure: little room for extra volume
  • Kidney failure or missed dialysis → think high potassium
  • Small children and older adults: small reserves, dry out fast
  • Deep, fast breathing may be compensation: check glucose, find the acid
slides.say: Now the things you never had to think about as an EMR. Listen to the lungs before and during a bolus, at least six sites on the front or the back. New crackles or harder breathing mean you pause and reassess before giving more. Patients with heart, kidney or liver failure often already carry extra fluid, so they have little room for more. Kidney failure or a missed dialysis should make you think of high potassium. Small children and older adults have small reserves and dry out quickly. And deep, fast breathing may be compensation: check the glucose and look for the source of the acid.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲你当 EMR 时不用想、现在要注意的事。推注补液前和补液中都要听肺，前胸或后背至少六个点。出现新的湿啰音或呼吸更费力，就先停下复评，再决定是否继续补。心、肾或肝衰竭的病人体内常常已经积液，几乎没有再加液体的空间。肾衰或漏做透析，要想到高钾。小孩和老人储备少，脱水很快。深而快的呼吸可能是代偿：测血糖，找出酸的来源。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Only 4.5% of body weight is in the vessels; isotonic fluid refills it — listen to the lungs
  2. Read the patient: kidney failure → potassium; breathing → acid–base
  3. Hypoxia injures cells fast; for vomiting losses the PCP adds IV, bolus, antiemetics

Next: shock inside the cell, immunity, inflammation and allergy
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: only a small share of body water is inside the vessels. Isotonic fluid refills that space without upsetting the cells, but listen to the lungs while you give it. Two: read the patient. Kidney failure or a missed dialysis should make you think of potassium, and the breathing pattern tells you the acid–base story. Three: hypoxia injures cells fast, and for fluid loss from vomiting, the PCP adds an IV, a fluid bolus and antiemetics. Next lesson, we'll look inside the shocked cell, and at immunity, inflammation and allergy. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，身体的水只有一小部分在血管里；等渗液能补充这个空间又不扰乱细胞，但补液时要听肺。二，读懂病人：肾衰或漏做透析要想到钾，呼吸方式会告诉你酸碱的情况。三，缺氧伤细胞很快；呕吐导致的丢液，PCP 多了静脉通路、推注补液和止吐药。下节课我们看休克时细胞里发生了什么，以及免疫、炎症和过敏。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
